- When sentiment is strongly bullish (≥0.8) in recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 2–5% for next 5–10 days.  
- When sentiment is strongly bearish (≤0.2) and prices are falling, model often underestimates the drop; adjust downward by 3–7% for next 7–14 days.  
- After a sharp price spike (≥5% from prior peak), model frequently overshoots; cap forecast at 10–15% below peak for 3–5 days.  
- If sentiment shifts from bullish to bearish within 3–5 days, model often fails to adjust; apply mean reversion bias: forecast = prior 5-day average + 0.5×(true - prior avg) for next 7 days.  
- For 30-day horizon, model consistently overestimates in high-sentiment periods; apply 1–3% downward correction if sentiment >0.6 for 3+ consecutive days.  
- If sentiment is neutral (0.2–0.6) and price is trending, model often lags; forecast should be adjusted upward by 1–3% for next 3–5 days if price is rising.
